memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'The priest shall burn them on the altar as a food offering presented to the LORD.'" - Lev 3:11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This short verse contains a phrase that could easily be misread: food offered to the LORD.

Israel's neighbours genuinely believed their gods needed feeding. Temples in the ancient world often functioned as kitchens for hungry deities. Israel's God was different, and He said so bluntly through the psalmist: "If I were hungry I would not tell you, for the world is mine, and all that is in it. Do I eat the flesh of bulls or drink the blood of goats?" (Ps 50:12-13).

So this is not God being fed. It is the language of a shared meal — God's portion set alongside the portions of the priest and the worshipper. The whole point of the fellowship offering was that God and His people were, in a manner of speaking, eating together.

That image runs right through Scripture and gathers into something glorious at the end. Jesus said He would drink again with His disciples in His Father's kingdom (Mtt 26:29). Revelation speaks of the wedding supper of the Lamb (Rev 19:9). To the lukewarm church, Christ says, "I will come in and eat with that person, and they with me" (Rev 3:20).

God has never needed our food. He has always wanted our company.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I imagine God as needing something from me, or as wanting me?
2. What would it mean to spend time with God today simply for His company?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You need nothing from me and yet You want me. Thank You for inviting me to Your table. Amen.
